Hi all,

Quick status and asks — NovaProd (RWI-2026-NOVA-0043) is on track for an upcoming procurement review but legal wants clarity on our proposed DPA posture before we lock the order form. I attached a one-page decision tree that maps the different paths (controller/processor roles, KMS ownership, SCCs vs. Transfer Addendum).

Can we do the following this week:
- Laura: confirm whether the redline in Exhibit A (roles table) can be accepted as-is or needs the alternative wording I sketched on p2 of the decision tree.
- Markus: confirm infra constraints on hosting regions and KMS key ownership (customer-managed vs. vendor-managed) — this changes the transfer impact path.
- Emily/purchasing@novaprod.com: please confirm if NovaProd expects the vendor to be a processor or a joint-controller for this use case. That will determine whether we need a transfer-addendum or the standard SCC switch.

Proposed 30-min sync: Tue 10:00 CET. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Attachments: rwi_dpa_decision_tree_v1.pdf, orderform_20260924_annotated.docx

Thanks,
Ben

From: Emily Wong <emily.wong@wonglegal.com>

Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 15:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: DPA decision tree + order form alignment — NovaProd

Thanks Ben — received and helpful framing. Quick points from NovaProd counsel’s side:

1) Role: NovaProd will be Controller for customer data; they asked that Redwood be documented as Processor. They flagged language in current Exhibit A that can be read as too broad ("processing purposes" list). We propose tightening the purpose language and adding a subprocessor notice cadence (30 days).

2) SCCs vs Transfer Addendum: They prefer starting with the European Commission SCCs and an Annex describing subprocessors and data export destinations. If there is any KMS/customer-key retention requirement that prevents us from exporting encrypted backups, they will want a short transfer-impact addendum.

3) Two redline files attached: novaprod_redlines_exhibitA.docx and a short markup showing the procurement team’s preferred signature block.

We can do Tue 10:00 CET; Emily and a procurement rep will join. Please note we redlined the Exhibit A role table and proposed explicit KMS language.

Regards,
Emily Wong
Wong Legal — Outside Counsel to NovaProd
Attachments: novaprod_redlines_exhibitA.docx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Emily Wong <emily.wong@wonglegal.com>
Cc: purchasing@novaprod.com
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:18:00 +0100
Subject: Re: DPA decision tree + order form alignment — NovaProd

Thanks Emily / Ben — reviewed the redlines this morning. High-level position we should take (summary, not final language):

- Roles: We accept Processor designation, but we will push back on any language that implies we act as Controller for customer-owned training or securely uploaded PII. I attached a short annotated order form with suggested replacement wording for Exhibit A (file: orderform_20260924_annotated.docx).
- SCCs: Agreed to apply the latest EC SCCs with a short Annex 1 that lists subprocessors and export locations. We will not sign a separate long-form transfer addendum unless NovaProd can confirm that customer-managed KMS prevents us from completing our standard backup/recovery workflows. If they insist on customer-managed keys that block encrypted export, we should fall back to a transfer-addendum path in the decision tree.
- Subprocessor notice: 30-day notice is reasonable, but we will retain a standard exception for emergency security responses (as usual).

Action items before Tue call:
1) Markus: confirm whether managed-backup exports can be performed in encrypted form without customer key escrow. If not, note which workflows are impacted.
2) Ben: please get a concrete statement from NovaProd on their KMS preference (vendor-managed vs customer-managed) before the call; procurement confirmation is sufficient.
3) I will prepare a short language packet (two paragraph alternatives) that we can agree on during the call.

I attached the annotated order form and a draft Exhibit A replacement. If everyone is aligned, I’ll prepare a single tracked-change document to send to Emily post-call.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: orderform_20260924_annotated.docx
